feedTitle: Shipping forecast for the North Irish Sea

items.title: Shipping forecast updated as of 23 October 2026 12:00pm
items.description:
##Current shipping forecast##

Valid for 24 HoursIssued on Friday, 23 October 2026 at 12:00pm by Ronaldsway Met Office
##Warning##

There is a Gale warning in operation.


##Synopsis##

A deep low (Storm Austen) lies in the eastern English Channel tracking eastwards, with associated frontal troughs affecting the Irish Sea, before a new rapidly deepening Atlantic low (Storm Boelo) tracks eastwards driving frontal troughs into the area by dawn on Saturday.


##Wind##

Northwest force 7 or gale 8, backing and decreasing west or northwest 6 or 7 this evening, and west or southwest 4 or 5 tonight, before starting to increase 5 or 6 by dawn on Saturday. Then increasing south 7 to severe gale 9 Saturday morning.


##State of Sea##

Moderate or rough, building mainly rough this afternoon, before starting to fall moderate or rough this evening and mainly moderate tonight. Then quickly building rough or very rough Saturday morning.


##Weather##

Heavy rain, turning lighter this afternoon before clearing to the east to become mainly fair by this evening. Then heavy rain spreading from the west from dawn on Saturday.


##Visibility##

Moderate or poor in heavy rain, becoming good for a time this evening & tonight.


##Outlook for the following 24 hours##


##Wind##

South force 7 to severe gale 9, veering west or southwest gale 8 or severe gale 9 later in the afternoon and into the evening, with little change overnight into Sunday.


##State of Sea##

Rough or very rough, becoming mainly very rough Saturday evening & overnight into Sunday.


##Weather##

Heavy rain clearing to the east later Saturday afternoon, leaving isolated showers.


##Visibility##

Moderate or poor in heavy rain, becoming moderate or good later Saturday afternoon.
